nodes.title: General prismatic envelopes over a bounded orientable prism
nodes.statement: Fix a bounded orientable prism (A,I), with I=(d). For any delta-A-algebra B and ideal J containing IB, construct a prism (C,IC) and a delta-map B→C carrying J into IC, initial among such maps to prisms over (A,I). Thus precomposition gives a bijection from prism maps C→T over A to delta-A-maps f:B→T satisfying f(J)⊆IT. No regularity, finite generation, completeness or flatness of B or J is assumed. The output is not asserted bounded or completely flat. The resulting functor on delta-pairs is independent of the chosen orientation up to its unique universal isomorphism.
hypotheses: p is prime; (A,I) is bounded and orientable; the generator d is used in the construction, not included in the resulting universal problem.
Targets may be unbounded prisms. The stronger source statement for an unbounded orientable base is not claimed by this bounded-base construction.
proofSteps: Adjoin delta-generators y_x for x∈J and impose d·y_x=x using the universal delta quotient. Maps of this algebra to a prism T over A correspond to maps B→T carrying J into dT, since d is a nonzerodivisor on T by rigidity.

In the category of delta-A-algebras, force d-torsion to vanish and then apply derived (p,d)-completion. Every map into a prism factors uniquely through both operations. The torsion-removal quotient must be universal in delta-rings; the ordinary d-torsion ideal need not be delta-stable.

Completion can reintroduce d-torsion. Follow Bhatt Lecture V Lemma 5.1: iterate torsion removal and derived completion transfinitely. The stabilization and smallness argument must preserve the universal mapping problem; at a limit of uncountable cofinality, countable inverse-limit equations for completeness commute with the filtered colimit. Do not replace this iteration by one quotient followed by one completion.

At the terminal stage establish discreteness, d-torsion-freeness and derived (p,d)-completeness, then invoke prism rigidity to obtain a prism. These are simultaneous obligations of the transfinite construction; no assertion that all intermediate derived completions are discrete is used. The detailed transfinite realization remains the explicit gap below.

For a completely regular kernel satisfying the separate regular-envelope hypotheses, identify both envelopes by their universal properties. Flatness and boundedness are imported only for that specialization.
acceptance: The universal property quantifies over unbounded targets as well as bounded ones; bounded output is a separate theorem.
A nonregular exactified kernel is permitted. Neither this target nor its source sketch implies complete flatness for that kernel.

uses.how: After exactification, supplies the ordinary envelope for the bounded orientable base case without a regular-kernel assumption.
Supplies existence in the A_inf-based initial prelog prism construction. The QRSP boundedness comparison still requires a separate regular-sequence reduction.

nodes.title: Quasi-coherent complexes on a prestack
nodes.statement: Let CRing be the category of commutative rings, and let X be a prestack: a functor from CRing to ∞-groupoids (for the uses here, to groupoids, such as Cart, WCart, WCart^HT, Spf A, BG for an affine group scheme G). Its category of points Pt(X) has objects the pairs (R, η) with η ∈ X(R), equivalently morphisms η : Spec R → X, and morphisms (R, η) → (R′, η′) the ring maps f : R → R′ with an identification X(f)(η) ≃ η′. Let D(R) be the derived ∞-category of R-modules with derived tensor product, and f^* = R′ ⊗^L_R (−) : D(R) → D(R′). The ∞-category of quasi-coherent complexes on X is the limit D(X) := lim_{(R, η) ∈ Pt(X)} D(R), formed in symmetric monoidal ∞-categories. An object F assigns to each point η a complex F_η ∈ D(R) and to each morphism an equivalence R′ ⊗^L_R F_η ≃ F_{η′}, with all higher coherences. Properties: (1) D(Spec R) ≃ D(R), F ↦ F_{id}; for the terminal prestack Spec Z, D(Spec Z) ≃ D(Z). (2) A morphism g : X → Y of prestacks induces a symmetric monoidal, exact, colimit-preserving pullback g^* : D(Y) → D(X), (g^*F)_η = F_{g∘η}, with id^* = id and (h∘g)^* ≃ g^* ∘ h^*. (3) D(X) is stable and admits small colimits, computed pointwise; it is presentable when X is a small colimit of corepresentable prestacks. (4) D sends small colimits of prestacks to limits: D(colim_i X_i) ≃ lim_i D(X_i). (5) A morphism of D(X) is an equivalence if and only if it is one at every point. (6) The unit O_X is (R, η) ↦ R; Perf(X) ⊂ D(X), the full subcategory of F with every F_η perfect, is exactly the subcategory of dualizable objects, and the invertible objects are those with every F_η invertible in D(R).
hypotheses: Fix nested universes and an essentially small ring/point indexing category in the universe used to form the limit. For a large prestack enlarge the universe; presentability is asserted in that universe only for a small colimit of representables. All rings in this node are ordinary commutative rings.

The limit is a limit of ∞-categories, not of the triangulated homotopy categories: gluing data must include all higher coherences, and the homotopy category of D(X) is not the limit of the homotopy categories of the D(R).

For a functor X defined only on rings in which p is nilpotent (a formal prestack over Spf Z_p, such as WCart), Pt(X) is formed over those rings; this is the same as D of the extension of X by the empty groupoid on the other rings, since the empty prestack has D = 0 (test below).
proofSteps: Construction: apply the straightening of the coCartesian fibration of pairs (R, M ∈ D(R)) over CRing to Pt(X), and take the ∞-category of coCartesian sections; equivalently the right Kan extension of R ↦ D(R) along the Yoneda embedding (Lurie, SAG Definition 6.2.2.1 and Remark 6.2.2.2, with Remark 6.2.2.7 for the pointwise description). The limits of presentable symmetric monoidal ∞-categories used are those of EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:presentability/limits-of-presentable-categories.
(1): Pt(Spec R) has the initial object (R, id), so the limit is evaluation there (SAG Remark 6.2.2.5); Spec Z is the terminal prestack because every ring receives a unique map from Z.

(2): precomposition of the limit diagram along Pt(X) → Pt(Y) (SAG Notation 6.2.2.6); (3): every D(R) is stable with colimits and every base change preserves them, so the limit is computed in the subcategory of stable ∞-categories with colimits and colimit-preserving functors (SAG Proposition 6.2.3.4 (1)–(3)).

(4): the right Kan extension of a functor turns colimits of presheaves into limits (SAG Lemma 6.2.1.12 as used in Proposition 6.2.3.1). (5): equivalences in a limit of ∞-categories are detected on the components.

Dualizability is detected componentwise in a limit of monoidal infinity-categories (HA Proposition 4.6.1.11, p.620). In D(R), finite sums, shifts, cones and retracts of R are dualizable. Conversely the duality formula for mapping out of M makes a dualizable M compact, and HA Proposition 7.2.4.4, p.1263 identifies compact modules with perfect modules. The module enhancement and scalar-change action are supplied by E1; its explicit duality comparison is a requested interface, not a consequence of the ordinary DerivedCategory name alone. Invertibility is likewise detected componentwise.
acceptance: For X = Spec R the construction returns D(R), and pullback along Spec R′ → Spec R is derived base change.
For X = WCart it returns Bhatt–Lurie's D(WCart) of Definition 3.3.1, with O_WCart the unit of Example 3.3.3.

For the classifying stack B(Z/2) over F_2 (the quotient of Spec F_2 by the trivial action of the constant group Z/2), Hom_{D(B(Z/2))}(O, O[1]) ≅ H^1(Z/2, F_2) = F_2, while the pullback to the atlas Spec F_2 kills it.

nodes.title: Complete modules on bounded-prism formal affines
nodes.statement: Fix a prime p and a bounded prism (A,I), and put J=(p)+I. Define Spf(A)(R) to be the set of continuous ring maps A→R when R has the discrete topology: equivalently, maps killing J^n for some n. Let D(Spf A) be the pointwise quasi-coherent infinity-category of PR.5/quasi-coherent-complexes-on-prestacks, on ordinary rings. There is a natural equivalence E_A:D(Spf A)≃D(A)^∧_J, where the right side is the full enhanced derived category of derived J-complete A-modules, with no cohomological boundedness restriction. Its inverse sends M to the family R⊗^L_A M at A→R. Under this equivalence the unit is A, tensor is M⊗̂^L_A N:=Λ_J(M⊗^L_A N), and colimits are Λ_J(colim_i M_i), where the inner colimit is formed in D(A). For a map of bounded prisms f:(A,I)→(B,IB), pullback corresponds to M↦Λ_(p,IB)(B⊗^L_A M). These equivalences respect identities, composition, units and tensor products, including all higher coherence. This is a formal-affine comparison, not an arbitrary nonflat ordinary-fibre-product base-change theorem.
hypotheses: The prism is bounded: A/I has bounded p-power torsion. The bounded-prism comparison is not extended here to an individual unbounded prism. I is an invertible Cartier ideal; one may work locally with I=(d).

D(A) and its completion are enhanced infinity-categories imported from E1 and DD.1. Ordinary adic completion of modules and the triangulated category alone are insufficient. Use the universe convention of the prestack construction.

For prism maps, rigidity identifies the target ideal with IB, hence the target topology is the one generated by the image of J. The displayed scalar-change formula is for these compatible ideals. A point A→R has nilpotent image of J, so no further completion is imposed on R⊗^L_A M.
proofSteps: The bounded-prism equivalence is the assertion immediately before BL22 Proposition 3.3.5, p.43; Warning 3.3.6 isolates its boundedness requirement. Since Spf A is the filtered colimit of Spec(A/J^n) on ordinary rings, the prestack limit construction identifies its category with lim_n D(A/J^n), with derived transition functors. Recovering every compatible unbounded system from its limit is an effectivity step; it is not a formal interchange of tensor and inverse limit. This proof refinement remains in the formal-affine gap.

Use DD.1/derived-completion and completion-exchanges for the reflective complete category, its completed colimits and tensor. SAG Corollary 8.2.4.15 and Remark 8.2.4.16, p.650 identify spectral formal QCoh with complete modules; Corollary 8.2.4.22 and Notation 8.2.4.23, pp.651–652 give completed tensor. They corroborate these operations but do not by themselves identify the ordinary-ring pointwise category used here.

Do not use SAG Theorem 8.3.4.4, pp.667–668 to discharge unbounded ordinary-ring effectivity: it compares connective spectral formal complexes, with almost-connective extension in Corollary 8.3.4.6. Remark 8.3.4.5 explicitly leaves the unrestricted spectral comparison open. The bounded-prism assertion in BL22 is the source for the stronger range in this node.

After effectivity is proved, evaluate the inverse comparison at every nilpotent ordinary test ring. Derived scalar-change associativity identifies pullback and tensor pointwise; DD.1 completion has the same reductions. Evaluation detects equivalences and supplies the coherent identity/composition laws. The unit is A since a bounded prism is derived J-complete. Complete-category colimits follow from the reflector, not from the raw inclusion into D(A).

For use in the WCart Cech presentation, combine this comparison with BL22 Lemma 3.3.10 and Corollary 3.3.11, p.44. The completed tensor transition formula is stated in the paragraph between them. Affineness of prism charts is Corollary 3.2.9, p.42; flatness for bounded prisms is equivalent to transversality by Corollary 3.2.10, pp.42–43. Keep that distinction when applying the separate flat affine pushforward theorem.

nodes.title: Faithfully flat descent for quasi-coherent complexes
nodes.statement: (1) Let R → S be a faithfully flat map of commutative rings, with Čech nerve S^• (S^n = S ⊗_R ⋯ ⊗_R S, n + 1 factors). Base change gives an equivalence of symmetric monoidal ∞-categories D(R) ≃ Tot(D(S^•)) = lim_{[n] ∈ Δ} D(S^n). (2) Consequently, for a morphism of prestacks u : X′ → X that becomes an equivalence after fpqc sheafification (in particular the canonical map X′ → (X′)^fpqc, with X = (X′)^fpqc), u^* : D(X) → D(X′) is an equivalence. (3) If X is an fpqc stack and U → X is a morphism of prestacks that is an effective epimorphism of fpqc sheaves (surjective fpqc-locally), with Čech nerve U_• (U_n the (n + 1)-fold fibre power over X), then D(X) ≃ Tot(D(U_•)); the same holds with the Zariski topology in place of the fpqc topology when U → X is a Zariski-local surjection. (4) On the hearts, (1) restricts to faithfully flat descent of modules.
hypotheses: (1): R → S faithfully flat, so every S^n is a discrete ring and every coface map is flat; for non-flat R → S the statement is false (test: Z → F_p).
(3): X is an fpqc (respectively Zariski) stack of ∞-groupoids on commutative rings; the fibre powers U_n need not be affine.

Use the universe convention of the construction node. Sheafification and effective epimorphisms of space-valued prestacks require the infinity-categorical extension requested from D0; its present groupoid stackification alone does not supply it.
proofSteps: (1) is the case of discrete rings and flat maps of Lurie's fpqc descent for module ∞-categories (SAG Corollary D.6.3.3); flatness keeps the Čech nerve discrete, so the relative tensor products agree with the ordinary ones.

(2): D sends colimits of prestacks to limits (PR.5/quasi-coherent-complexes-on-prestacks (4)); by (1) the functor Spec R ↦ D(R) is an fpqc sheaf of ∞-categories, so D factors through fpqc sheafification (the argument of SAG Proposition 6.2.3.1 and Remark 6.2.3.2).

(3): an effective epimorphism of sheaves is the geometric realization of its Čech nerve, so X ≃ |U_•| after sheafification; apply (2) and the limit property (4) of the construction node. This is the descent step of Bhatt–Lurie Lemma 3.3.10 (Zariski) and of the proof of Proposition 3.3.5 (flat).
(4): truncate to discrete objects and compare with SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/qcoh-fpqc-descent.
acceptance: For X = WCart and the Zariski surjection Spf(A^0) → WCart with fibre powers Spf(A^n), (3) gives Bhatt–Lurie's equivalence D(WCart) ≃ Tot(D̂(A^•)) (Lemma 3.3.10). Here D(Spf A) is the derived (p,I)-complete module category, not D(A). The formal-affine identification and completed scalar change are the explicit formal-QCoh gap of this review.
For a finite Galois extension of fields K → L with group G, (1) and (3) give D(K) ≃ D(L)^{hG}, the ∞-categorical form of Galois descent.
Non-example: for Z → F_p (not flat), Tot(D(F_p^{⊗•})) is not D(Z); for instance Q is killed by base change.

nodes.title: Flat affine direct image, base change and projection formula
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be a flat affine morphism of prestacks on ordinary commutative rings: each fibre Y ×_X Spec R is Spec B_η with B_η flat over R, and ordinary pullback gives B_η ⊗_R R′. Then (a) f^* has a right adjoint f_*, whose value at η is the restriction to Spec B_η regarded as an R-complex; (b) g^* f_* ≃ f′_* g′^* for every base change g : X′ → X; and (c) f_* preserves small colimits and F ⊗ f_*G ≃ f_*(f^*F ⊗ G). These three assertions are about flat affine maps in this discrete-prestack setting. Independently, (d) if D(X) is presentable in the chosen universe, M ↦ M ⊗ O_X from D(Z) to D(X) has a right adjoint RΓ(X,−). For an effective fpqc or Zariski Čech presentation, RΓ(X,F) is the totalization of the global sections of its restrictions. On formal affine charts, use derived complete module categories and completed tensor products under the separately recorded formal-QCoh interface.
hypotheses: Each B_η is flat over R. Without this, an ordinary pullback B ⊗_R R′ need not compute B ⊗^L_R R′. SAG uses spectral prestacks and derived fibre products, so its arbitrary base-change theorem is not an arbitrary ordinary-ring base-change theorem.

For (d), presentability and the universe bound are hypotheses, not automatic assertions for every large prestack. On the formal Čech presentation of WCart, use the complete module categories of BL22 Lemma 3.3.10 and Corollary 3.3.11.
proofSteps: For R → B flat, B ⊗^L_R R′ = B ⊗_R R′, so associativity identifies R′ ⊗^L_R M with (B ⊗_R R′) ⊗^L_B M. The restrictions of G to affine fibres therefore form a Cartesian family of R-complexes. The adjunction is the limit of these coherent pointwise scalar-extension/restriction adjunctions.

Pointwise restriction of scalars preserves colimits and satisfies the projection formula. Evaluation detects the resulting equivalences. SAG Proposition 6.3.4.1 and Corollary 6.3.4.3, pp.505–507, supply the derived setting; flatness permits this discrete specialization.

For (d), apply the presentable adjoint theorem to the colimit-preserving tensor-with-unit functor. Under Čech descent mapping spaces and the pointwise global-section adjunctions identify its right adjoint with the totalization. This argument does not require the atlas maps U_n → X themselves to be affine. BL22 Corollary 3.3.11 gives the WCart instance.
acceptance: For a bounded transversal prism, ρ_A : Spf(A) → WCart is flat affine (BL22 Corollary 3.2.10, pp.42–43). The flat affine theorem applies on ordinary-ring points; its expression in complete A-modules additionally uses the formal-QCoh interface. Affineness of an arbitrary bounded prism is insufficient for the pointwise base-change claim.
For WCart, BL22 Corollary 3.3.11 computes RΓ as Tot(M^•) on its universal oriented-prism Čech presentation, with a derived p-complete result.

Tor counterexample to the discarded nonflat assertion: R = Z, B = R′ = F_p and M = F_p. The ordinary fibre algebra is F_p; the left side F_p ⊗^L_Z F_p has H^(−1) = F_p while the right side F_p ⊗^L_F_p F_p does not.
Flat check: Z → Z[1/ℓ] and R′ = F_p give restriction/base-change compatibility, including zero when ℓ = p.

nodes.title: Framed algebras and their q-automorphisms
nodes.statement: Put t = q − 1 in a commutative coefficient ring D and I = (t) or (p,t). Let P be an ordinary D-algebra, classically and derived I-complete, with an I-completely ind-étale polynomial or toric framing D[X_s]^∧_I → P. Require that the completed framing source is discrete, that P/tP and P/(tX_s)P are classically I-complete, and that every tX_s is a nonzerodivisor. Then there are unique D-algebra automorphisms γ_s that scale X_s by q, fix the other coordinates and reduce to the identity modulo t. They commute, and γ_s(f) − f belongs to tX_sP. Continuous D-algebra maps with an injective coordinate map intertwine these automorphisms; automorphisms in extra target directions fix the image. If D and P are p-torsion-free, P/pP is classically I-complete, D is a δ-ring with δ(q)=0, and I=(p,t), P has the unique compatible δ-structure with δ(X_s)=0, and its Frobenius commutes with the γ_s. These are sufficient hypotheses for the completed variant, rather than a claim about all merely p-completely ind-étale framings. The completion topologies used by the sources are compared by the following cofinal-power formulas: J=(p,[p]_q)⊆K=(p,q−1), K^(p−1)⊆J; for q=(1+u)^p and ξ=[p]_(1+u), K⊆H=(p,ξ) and H^p⊆K.
hypotheses: All coefficient automorphisms are D-linear and hence fix q. Polynomial completion is taken at I; in the toric variant the coordinates are units. Modulo every I^n the framing is ind-étale.

Classical completeness of P and the listed quotients is imposed so reduction and compatible infinitesimal lifts recover actual maps and principal-ideal divisibility. It is not inferred from the words derived complete alone. Extending this sufficient formulation to every general-base consumer remains a gap.
The parameter q is a unit in the I-completed framing source and in P because t ∈ I; D itself need not be complete or contain q^(−1).
The δ assertion needs p-torsion-freeness of P as well as D, and classical I-completeness of P/pP to detect divisibility by p after infinitesimal lifting. I contains p and φ(t)=q^p−1 belongs to I.

For prime p and t=q−1 in any commutative ring, put J=(p,[p]_q) and K=(p,t). Then J⊆K and K^(p−1)⊆J, hence K^((p−1)n)⊆J^n⊆K^n for every n. For u with q=(1+u)^p and ξ=[p]_(1+u), put H=(p,ξ). Then t=uξ, K⊆H and H^p⊆K, hence H^(pn)⊆K^n⊆H^n. These are cofinal ideal filtrations, not equal ideals. They identify the classical completions of every module and the corresponding continuous maps. For derived completion, use DD.1/ordinary-quotient-completion only after verifying its regular-sequence or other comparison hypotheses for both ideals. In A_inf(O_C), u=[ε^(1/p)]−1 and ξ generates ker θ; both p and the nonzero reductions of u,t,ξ are regular, so the regular-pair comparison applies. This argument neither gives a merely p-adic framing nor proves completeness of P/(tX_s).
proofSteps: On the completed polynomial algebra scale one coordinate by q. The inverse scales it by q^(−1), which exists in the completed source. The difference on a monomial is divisible by tX_s; the same formula holds on toric monomials.

For each n, ind-étaleness modulo I^n lifts the identity modulo I uniquely along the nilpotent I/I^n thickening, with the changed polynomial structure map. Take the compatible limit in the classically I-complete algebra P. Applying the same uniqueness modulo t proves reduction to the identity. Uniqueness proves commutation and the inverse formula. This is the completed-lifting argument of SQDEF §3, pp.6–7, with the extra quotient-completeness hypotheses stated here.

To obtain divisibility, repeat uniqueness in P/(tX_s,I^n), where the altered coordinate map is the identity. Completeness of P/(tX_s) identifies the inverse limit with this quotient, so γ_s acts as the identity there. For coordinate-injective maps compare the two induced lifts; an extra target direction has the unchanged polynomial map, hence fixes the image.

For the δ assertion, put the framed Frobenius on the source: φ_D on coefficients and X_s↦X_s^p. Modulo I this is Frobenius; since φ(I)⊆I, unique ind-étale infinitesimal lifting extends it through each P/I^n and then to P. Compare modulo (p,I^n) with the characteristic-p Frobenius; completeness of P/pP gives φ_P(f)≡f^p modulo p. Dividing by p in the p-torsion-free P gives the unique δ-structure (PR.0/delta-ring-category). Its compatibility with the source and γ_s follows from δ(q)=δ(X_s)=0 and uniqueness of the same lifts. The ordinary delta-etale-extension node motivates this argument but is not being asserted to supply the completed extension without these hypotheses.

The topology comparison is elementary: modulo p, [p]_q=t^(p−1). Thus J⊆K and every degree-(p−1) monomial in p,t lies in J. In the cyclotomic case the geometric-sum identity gives t=uξ, while modulo p one has t=u^p and ξ=u^(p−1), so ξ^p=t^(p−1) modulo p and H^p⊆K. Raise these inclusions to powers. Cofinal inverse systems give the classical module-completion comparison. For A_inf, p-torsion-freeness and the domain O_C^♭ identify the two generating pairs as regular; invoke the stated DD.1 ordinary-quotient comparison for derived completions. The identities compare topology only; do not transport a regular quotient or an ind-étale framing without checking it.
acceptance: For P = D[X]^∧ with one coordinate, γ(X^m) = q^m X^m for m ≥ 0.
Modulo q − 1 every γ_s is the identity, so all structure collapses to the plain framed algebra P/(q − 1).

sources.locator: Constructions 16.19–16.20 and footnote 21, pp.114–115; Notation 17.1, p.117 of arXiv:1905.08229v4
sources.match: The source treats A-flat q-PD bases and p-complete framed algebras. It motivates the operators, but its stated p-only extension is not the proof of this strengthened I-complete variant; inherited source issue E65 and the p-only counterexample remain relevant. Notation 17.1 fixes the A_inf cyclotomic q and ξ=φ^(-1)([p]_q); it does not identify the corresponding ideals as equal.

The t-adic framing construction is in §3; §4, p.9 gives q=[ε], u=[ε^(1/p)]−1, ξ=[p]_(1+u), and (p,ξ)-completed A_inf frames. The cofinal-power bounds in this node are derived explicitly from these formulas; they are not attributed as a separately stated source theorem.

nodes.title: q-derivatives and the framed q-de Rham Koszul complex
nodes.statement: Let D → E be a map of commutative rings, q ∈ D, X_s ∈ E and γ_s commuting D-algebra automorphisms with γ_s(X_t)=q^(δ_st)X_t, γ_s(f)−f ∈ (q−1)X_sE, and each (q−1)X_s a nonzerodivisor. For any set S, the unique quotients ∇_(q,s) defined by (q−1)X_s∇_(q,s)(f)=γ_s(f)−f are D-linear, obey the twisted Leibniz law, satisfy ∇_(q,s)(X_s^n)=[n]_q X_s^(n−1) for n≥1 and commute pairwise. For finite S their cochain Koszul complex has qΩ^i = E ⊗_D Λ^i(D^S), in degrees 0 through |S|, and differential fω ↦ Σ_s ∇_(q,s)(f)dX_s∧ω. It is linear over the common γ-invariants. For infinite S the separate completed-q-derivative-summability target gives a construction under an explicit decay condition; verifying decay for every inherited consumer remains a gap. A coordinate-injective D-algebra map gives a chain map if it intertwines matching γ_s and all extra target directions fix its image. For a finite complete étale framing as in the previous node, with flat coefficients and the completed reduction identified with the framed special fibre, reduction modulo q−1 is its continuous relative de Rham complex. For unit coordinates the change of basis dX_s = X_s dlog X_s identifies the complex with the Koszul complex of (γ_s−1)/(q−1), hence with η_(q−1) of the complex of γ_s−1. Finally, if φ commutes with γ_s, φ(q)=q^p and φ(X_s)=X_s^p, then ∇_(q,s)φ=[p]_q X_s^(p−1)φ∇_(q,s).
hypotheses: The automorphisms fix the coefficient ring D, including q. For qΩ impose finite S, or the separately specified continuity and summability conditions; the exact quotient operators alone impose no summability.

The differential γ_s−1 is divisible by t, so the degree-i submodule of η_t of its Koszul complex is exactly t^i times the degree-i term; multiplication by t^i identifies the divided-operator complex with it. This directly establishes the required special case of the AI.1 décalage construction. For Frobenius apply φ to the quotient equation and cancel tX_s, using φ(tX_s)=t[p]_q X_s^p.

nodes.title: Summability of q-derivatives in completed coordinate modules
nodes.statement: Let E be a classically I-adically complete separated D-algebra, with I a finitely generated ideal of D, and let (q,X_s,γ_s)_(s∈S) be the regular q-derivation datum of q-derivations-and-their-koszul-complex. Require the decay condition: for every f∈E and n≥1, ∇_s(f)∈I^nE for all but finitely many s. Define completed q-forms in degree i as lim_n ⊕_(F⊂S finite, |F|=i) (E/I^nE)e_F, using an auxiliary total order for wedge signs. They form a cochain complex with d(f e_F)=Σ_s ∇_s(f)e_s∧e_F, independent of the order by the canonical exterior-basis change. Finite S recovers the finite Koszul complex, because E is complete. A continuous D-algebra map with an injective coordinate map intertwining matching γ_s and fixed image under extra target γ_u induces a chain map of completed complexes. A sufficient criterion for decay is: some c≥0 satisfies (I^(n+c)E:tX_s)⊆I^nE uniformly in s,n≥1, and for every f,n the differences γ_s(f)−f lie in I^(n+c)E for all but finitely many s. Here t=q−1. The standard completed polynomial and Laurent charts over Z[[t]] with I=(t), or Z_p[[t]] with I=(p,t), satisfy this criterion with c=1. No assertion that every completed ind-étale algebra or q-PD envelope satisfies it is made without verification.
hypotheses: I is pulled back from D. D-linearity implies ∇_s(I^nE)⊆I^nE uniformly in s, so each induced quotient operator is well-defined. Individual continuity without decay is insufficient.

The completed forms use the inverse-limit topology with kernels of projection to level n. No assertion that arbitrary ordinary quotients of a complete module are complete is used. The complex is D-linear; a usual commutative DGA product is not asserted.

For standard charts, first establish the uniform colon estimate from injectivity of multiplication by the initial form of tX_s in the associated graded ring. A general change of coefficient ring requires rechecking that estimate.

AI.1 owns the generic commuting-operator complex and its completion interface. This target checks the q-specific convergence contract and charts; it does not create a second generic Koszul theory. DD.2 continuous forms are used only in their stated finite smooth range.
proofSteps: Regular division gives the q-operators and their pairwise commutation by the preceding target. At level n, decay makes d(f e_F) a finite sum, and D-linearity makes it independent of the chosen lift of f modulo I^n. Extend linearly to the finite-support degree-i module. The two orders of every distinct pair of operators cancel by their wedge signs, while repeated indices wedge to zero. Thus d_n²=0, including in characteristic two. The quotient operators commute with transition maps; take the degreewise inverse limit. No interchange of cohomology with inverse limit is used.

The algebraic exterior module is dense in these completed forms. The differentials preserve each projection kernel, so the formula extends uniquely and continuously. For finite S each degree has finitely many basis vectors and completion returns the finite Koszul terms over E.

For maps, regular-quotient uniqueness intertwines matching derivatives; extra-direction fixed-image hypotheses make the additional terms zero. At every quotient level the induced wedge map takes finite support to finite support. Pass to the inverse limit, obtaining identity and composition compatibilities.

For the sufficient criterion, divide γ_s(f)−f=tX_s∇_s(f) using the uniform colon inclusion. In a standard polynomial or Laurent chart, approximate f modulo I^(n+1) by a polynomial with finitely many coordinates. Every other γ_s fixes that approximation. The associated graded ring is Z[X_s][T] for I=(t), or F_p[X_s][P,T] for I=(p,t), with coordinates inverted in the Laurent case. Multiplication by TX_s is injective and raises filtration by one, proving (I^(n+1):tX_s)⊆I^n uniformly. Completeness and separatedness exclude an element of infinite nonzero filtration order.

For a completed ind-étale or q-PD-envelope consumer, separately prove finite-coordinate approximation and the uniform division estimate, or prove decay directly on a dense generating family and use the uniform filtration bound. Regularity of each tX_s by itself supplies no uniform estimate. These consumer verifications remain in the complete-framing gap.

nodes.title: The Beilinson fibre square on syntomic complexes (named input)
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R write Q_p(n)(R) = Z_p(n)(R)[1/p] for the syntomic complex of PR.4/syntomic-complex, LΩ_R for the p-completed derived de Rham cohomology of R over Z_p with its Hodge filtration LΩ_R^{≥n} (not Hodge-completed), and (−)_{Q_p} for p-completion followed by inverting p. (i) For every p-torsion-free quasisyntomic ring R and n ≥ 0 there are a natural map χ_n : Q_p(n)(R/p) → (LΩ_R)_{Q_p} and a functorial pullback square in D(Q_p) with top row Q_p(n)(R) → Q_p(n)(R/p), left column Q_p(n)(R) → (LΩ_R^{≥n})_{Q_p}, right column χ_n and bottom row (LΩ_R^{≥n})_{Q_p} → (LΩ_R)_{Q_p}; equivalently a fibre sequence Q_p(n)(R) → Q_p(n)(R/p) → (LΩ_R/LΩ_R^{≥n})_{Q_p}. (ii) For R quasiregular semiperfectoid and p-torsion-free and n > 0, χ_n is injective with image the φ = p^n eigenspace of A_crys(R/p)[1/p] = (LΩ_R)_{Q_p}; up to a nonzero scalar depending only on n it is the forgetful map Q_p(n)(R/p) → Δ_{R/p}[1/p] composed with Δ_{R/p} ≅ A_crys(R/p) ≅ LΩ_R. (iii) Check: for R = O_C the sequence on H^0 is 0 → Q_p(n) → (B_crys^+)^{φ = p^n} → B_dR^+/Fil^n → 0 for n ≥ 1. Within this roadmap the statement is a named input: its only consumer, PR.7/tate-twist-analytic-continuation, is proved from it, and its proof (through topological cyclic homology) lies outside the roadmaps this roadmap builds on.
hypotheses: R p-torsion-free and quasisyntomic in (i); quasiregular semiperfectoid in (ii); n ≥ 0 in (i), n > 0 in (ii).
The order of operations in (−)_{Q_p} matters: complete first, then invert p.

This roadmap does not prove the statement: the proof constructs the square from the pullback square TC(R; Q_p) → TC(R/p; Q_p) over HC^-(R; Q_p) → HP(R; Q_p) and the motivic filtrations of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, which no roadmap below this one in the upstream order provides; the gap 'Trace-theoretic proof of the Beilinson fibre square' records it.

Quasisyntomic includes p-adic completeness and bounded torsion as in DD.5. AMMN qSyn_Zp here is the p-torsion-free subcategory. A_crys(R/p) ≃ LΩ_R and the comparison between trace-defined and prismatic syntomic objects are interfaces recorded as gaps until supplied in this tier.
proofSteps: Outline of the source proof, for the record of the named input: for R quasiregular semiperfectoid the bottom row of the TC/HC^-/HP square is even, so τ_{[2n−1, 2n]} of the square is again a pullback; by the definition of Z_p(n) through the motivic filtration and the description of π_{2n}HC^- and π_{2n}HP by Hodge-completed derived de Rham cohomology this gives a Hodge-completed version of the square; Hodge completion is removed by left Kan extension from polynomial algebras; general quasisyntomic R follows by unfolding (Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus, Theorem 6.17 with proof).

(ii): Proposition 6.18 of the same paper, using Corollary 6.20, the Frobenius action of Lemma 6.19 and the scalar-endomorphism argument of Proposition 6.21; the identification of their Z_p(n) (defined with topological cyclic homology) with the prismatic syntomic complex is Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 14.1 with Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Theorem 1.12.

(iii): for R = O_C, Q_p(n)(O_C) = Q_p(n)[0] by the étale comparison PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison, Q_p(n)(O_C/p) has H^0 = (A_crys(O_C/p)[1/p])^{φ = p^n} = (B_crys^+)^{φ = p^n} and LΩ_{O_C}/Fil^n ⊗ Q = B_dR^+/Fil^n (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4/rational-hodge-period-comparison).
acceptance: For R = O_C and n = 1: 0 → Q_p(1) → (B_crys^+)^{φ = p} → C → 0, the fundamental exact sequence.
For n = 0 the third term vanishes and the square says Q_p(0)(R) ≃ Q_p(0)(R/p).
Consumed exactly once: PR.7/tate-twist-analytic-continuation, steps 2–3.

nodes.title: Triviality of the slope-zero bundle of a weakly admissible module (named input)
nodes.statement: Let K be complete discretely valued of characteristic zero with perfect residue field k, C the completion of a chosen algebraic closure of K, F=C^♭ and E=Q_p. Let X_sch be the schematic Fargues–Fontaine curve of F with the untilt point ∞ determined by C, and ℛ the Robba ring of FF Definition 1.8.1. The named input comprises: (i) vector bundles on X_sch correspond to Frobenius-equivariant analytic bundles on Y through GAGA (FF Theorem 11.3.1), and these correspond to finite free ℛ-modules with invertible semilinear φ (Corollary 11.2.22); (ii) for a weakly admissible filtered φ-module D over K_0=W(k)[1/p], with D_K=D⊗_(K_0)K, the modification of E(D) at ∞ defined by the B_dR^+-lattice Fil^0(D_K⊗_K B_dR) is semistable of slope zero (Proposition 10.5.6); and (iii) every slope-zero semistable bundle on X_sch is O_(X_sch)^r (Theorem 8.2.10(1)). Consequently its Robba φ-module has a φ-fixed basis. Transport to the adic quotient curve supplied by AdicSpaces requires the analytic/schematic dictionary, point ∞, Robba-ring normalization and construction matching specified in the gap. These are named inputs for PR.7/weakly-admissible-extension-over-ainf, rather than a supplied classification theorem of AdicSpaces.
hypotheses: C is the completed algebraic closure of K in the source of the weak-admissibility assertion; the algebraically closed tilt is essential for the slope classification.

Use the usual filtered φ-module convention D_K=D⊗_(K_0)K and N=0. The Frobenius-twisted scalar convention of the prismatic consumer must be matched explicitly, not identified silently. R06.2 presently has a finite-extension field range; its perfect-residue-field extension is a precise supplier request.

The schematic curve, its untilt point and bundles are part of this named interface. AdicSpaces supplies only the adic quotient construction. GAGA and compatibility of the period modification with the particular Robba module of the consumer remain recorded proof/construction gaps.
proofSteps: Use FF Theorem 11.3.1 (pp.330–331) to pass from schematic bundles to analytic Frobenius-equivariant bundles, then Corollary 11.2.22 (p.328) for the Robba-module equivalence. Specify the radius normalization and tensor-compatible dictionary in the supplier interface.

FF Proposition 10.5.6 (p.290), under the Chapter 10 setup (p.264), identifies the Harder–Narasimhan filtrations of the filtered module and its modified bundle. Weak admissibility gives slope zero. FF Theorem 8.2.10(1) (p.238) then trivializes this schematic bundle.

Under the equivalence the trivial rank-r bundle is the rank-r module with its standard φ, so it has a φ-fixed basis. To use this on PR.7/weakly-admissible-extension-over-ainf one must identify that consumer’s analytic continuation with this modification; BS23-FCRYS §6.4 p.26 asserts the matching and the inherited packet already records its proof as a gap.
acceptance: For D = K_0 with φ_D = σ and the trivial filtration, the bundle is O_X and the φ-module is ℛ with its Frobenius: trivially trivial.

For D = D_cris(V) of a crystalline representation V (for instance V = Q_p(1), D = K_0 e with φ(e) = p^{-1}e and Fil^{-1} = D_K, Fil^0 = 0), the modified bundle is V ⊗_{Q_p} O_X, trivial of slope 0, as (ii)–(iii) predict.
